column1: # The routes and what must hold on each replay: tools/check_routes.py (ctest oracles-routes, with ORACLES_ROM_DIR set).

# overworld.route with the sub-pixel camera in the drawn-back view: leaving a house through its edge, the scroll's start opens the room the band showed whole and widens its bounds, and the camera moved toward Link by a pixel before the game's window moved or the warp cut in, the band easing down by it (a player saw the house rise by a pixel on leaving it); the band now stands where it stood until the window moves: at 4x it moves on none of the 51 such frames instead of 12 (enhanced.alone_scroll_band_moves). The band is held at the camera of the frame before, not moved back to it by its fraction, which showed a black line over the house's top row: that row is cut on none of those frames instead of all 51 (enhanced.alone_scroll_cut_frames). Leaving the rooms of two-room interiors (3:f8, 2:eb), not shown whole, the camera moved down by up to 3 px before the warp; from a room the camera stood still in, the game still in it, the band now stands there too: 85 such frames, the band moving on none.

# Link's sprite as drawn goes back on the screen twice in overworld.route (enhanced.link_backsteps_y): a pose a few pixels higher while the camera steps, and a knockback of two pixels a frame the camera's catch-up steps ahead of. Without the sub-pixel camera the band steps with his whole steps, its stops between two of them and its steps back across a diagonal held at what they are (enhanced.band_stops, enhanced.band_wobble).

# overworld.route in the drawn-back view without the sub-pixel camera: leaving a house, the whole-pixel camera stepped by a pixel as the exit opened the room's edge, the house's top row cut out of the band on all 51 of those frames from rooms shown whole and the band moving on 5 of the 85 frames counted with the two-room interiors; it is held as with the sub-pixel camera, still on all of them (enhanced.alone_scroll_band_moves, enhanced.alone_scroll_cut_frames).
# overworld.route in the far view fitted to the screen (--screen): 426x320 on 1280x960, 412x360 on 1240x1080, the rules of its far 4:3 rows.
# overworld.route in the view's other sizes (docs/REFERENCE.md): near in 4:3, medium in 16:9 and 4:3.

# overworld.route with the status bar drawn full width (--hud full, the launcher's default hud=full): the bands beside it take its own background on every line of every world frame, in the near, far and far 4:3 views.

# overworld.route in the far view with the status bar full width and the hotbar, as the launcher plays by default: at every door (Lynna's shop, the houses) the load keeps the band as in play, bar, background and slots, and the play area where the world shows it before and after (enhanced.load_band_changes, enhanced.load_area_moves).

# overworld.route with the item hotkeys' slots and F3 (--framed-toggle-at) at 1500 and back to the wide world at 6000: the framed core, as in Faithful, never shows the hotbar, the room changes and their loads included (enhanced.hotbar_framed_only_frames, 602 frames before), and the wide world shows it again after.

# With the ghosts' order running the other side of Ages' sea from the room there, the ghost reaches the row beyond it once more before Link moves on, and 3:f0, refused like every time as a capture caught in a fade, is counted once more: 11 runs failed (enhanced.ghost_failed), 10 before.
# advanced.route reloaded in near 4:3 and medium 4:3: the state saved and restored at those sizes.
# advanced.route with the status bar drawn full width: the bands follow the bar through the time warps' dark and white fades, the sea and a dungeon of the past.

# dungeon-sideview.route with the sub-pixel camera: a dungeon's large rooms keep the game's window, Link drawn at his fraction of a pixel there; the side views keep his whole pixels. At 6766, in 4:72, pushed back as he walks right, his step changes by 9 px, his fraction drawn from that frame: counted as a switch, where before it counted elsewhere (enhanced.link_jolt_max, 16).
# dungeon-sideview.route in near 4:3: the side-view rooms, larger than the band, followed with the game's window.
# dungeon-sideview.route with the status bar drawn full width: a dungeon's large rooms and its side-view rooms.
# underwater.route in medium 16:9: the band wider than a room reaches the sea, as the drawn-back view does.
# mermaid-hold.route: underwater.route's start replayed with the swim's hold (its header's option), then directions held on the sea floor.

# mermaid-hold.route with the transitions' swim and diagonal: its start, underwater.route's on foot, holds diagonals through some of its scrolls, which the diagonal carries: the game parts from the recording at 1173, carried along the bottom edge into 0:67, and stays on land in group 0 to the end, the directions meant for the sea floor held on foot; its carries and the walls across holding Link (transitions.carried_frames, carry_withheld_frames) are walking crossings.  seafloor-diagonal.route crosses the sea floor's edges.

# mermaid-hold-set.route: mermaid-hold.route with the swim's hold changed while the game runs by `set swim-hold` lines (format 10), as the pause's Swimming writes them: off at 3060, on again at 3140.  The 21 strokes before 3060 are mermaid-hold.route's, the hold starts none while it is off where mermaid-hold.route starts 7, and 15 once it is on again.

# mermaid-hold-window.route: mermaid-hold.route with the window changed while the game runs by `set window` lines (format 10), as the pause's Window writes them: presentation alone, the game and the Enhanced run mermaid-hold.route's (its run hash).

# seafloor-diagonal.route: Link on Ages' sea floor in his mermaid suit, crossing the edges of 2:b7, 2:b6, 2:a6 and 2:a7 diagonally, written by hand with the transitions' swim and diagonal and the swim's hold: tapped left into 2:b6 and up-left into 2:a6, held down-right back into 2:b6, up-right into 2:b7 and 2:a7; his motion carries him across the scroll's axis whether a direction is held or not, from the first frame the room entered's collisions are loaded (transitions.carried_frames and carry_withheld_frames, with those of its start); the one vertical camera jump is the start's, as on mermaid-hold.route.

# seafloor-diagonal.route with the sub-pixel camera: the sea floor's waves draw each line at its own scroll; Link is drawn apart there too, the window rendered again without him at each line's scroll, and the band takes its fraction under the waves as elsewhere, where it kept whole pixels and turned the scenery around him, stepping on x and y in turn: at 4x it stops between two of its steps 11 times an axis instead of 116 and goes back across the swim by 2 px or more 6 times instead of 81 (enhanced.band_stops, enhanced.band_wobble), the layer on 2727 frames instead of 2018, none refused, nothing left or wrong, and Link's own fraction kept with the band's, so that he never moves against the ground at a scroll (enhanced.transition_layer_shift_max). On the course the prediction of the room entered's collisions gives, the scroll down into 2:b7 ends as a stroke of the suit does: the game then moves Link by 1.125 px every other frame (0, then 2 px), and the band, still easing out of the scroll by three quarters of a pixel a frame, has his sprite go back up on the screen by a pixel once (frame 2725, enhanced.link_backsteps_y, on both cores), where the camera of whole pixels, following his, steps the band instead.

# seafloor-diagonal.route reloaded at 3122, in the scroll up into 2:a6 that carries Link across: the savestate keeps the transitions' progress, and the 14 frames after the load to the scroll's end put him where the run before the load did (enhanced.reload_transition_differing), none of them left to the machine alone (transitions.resumed_frames); the neighbours never come back to the natural arrival's, the route's inputs taking Link elsewhere after the load.

# hotkeys-use.route with the sub-pixel camera (--enhanced-subpixel): Ages' items used by the hotkeys; Link drawn apart with what stands at his fraction of a pixel alone, the objects at their own left to the band (enhanced.subpixel_objects_off).

# hotkeys-use.route with the hotbar's four slots: each icon found in the ROM's tables from the start of play, as the status bar would draw the item on a button (enhanced.hotbar_icons_decoded, the distinct icons), and found again each time the bar reloads its icons, the hotbar arming that hook with or without the hotkeys' policy (enhanced.hotbar_icons_refound), and checked against the screen while the item is on B or A (enhanced.hotbar_icons_checked, enhanced.hotbar_icon_wrong).

# hotkeys-use-set.route: hotkeys-use.route with the item hotkeys off at 11000 and on again at 11900 by `set item-hotkeys` lines (format 10), as the pause's Item hotkeys writes them: notes, the exchanges being the route's `equip` lines; the game and the Enhanced run hotkeys-use.route's (its run hash).

# hotkeys-throw.route with the item hotkeys' live policy in `use` and scripted keys: the bombs' key lifts a bomb at 1950 and throws it at 1995, as B does; the power bracelet's key picks it up from the ground at 2018 and throws it at 2048; the bombs' key lifts another at 2200 and the feather's key throws it at 2240, nothing exchanged, no jump: while Link holds something over his head, any item button throws it, a press of its own and not a use (hotkeys.live.throw_presses).  Before, the second press waited for a button the game reads no item on while Link holds, and was dropped (hotkeys.live.throws=0, the bomb going off in his hands).  A use borrows its button without the equip sound.

# hotkeys-throw-recorded.route: the same session recorded, its throws `throw` lines: on replay each lets Link go of what he held (hotkeys.throws, hotkeys.throw_not_thrown), and no use is left unfired, where a throw noted as a use of the button's item would count one.

# hotkeys-throw.route in `equip`: each item the keys equip, and the item a key already equipped gives back, sounds as the inventory's equip does (snd_selectitem through playSound, from the next frame's start).
# hotkeys-equip-sound.route: that session recorded (format 14), its `sound` lines handed to the game at their frames on replay: the same game as the session, which the sound changes from 1951 on.

# hotkeys-inventory-sound.route: a hotkey's key on the item under the inventory's cursor, recorded; its `sound` line runs with the menu still open (hotkeys.sounds_in_inventory), where the call transaction waited for the menu to close before.
# hotkeys-use.route with the hotbar on the status bar drawn full width: the slots drawn over the bar's own background, nothing else touched.
# hotkeys-use.route in near 4:3, whose gutters are too narrow for the hotbar (none drawn, no icon captured, the hotkeys working), and with the hotbar in medium 4:3.
# zoom-out.route drawn back: the dungeon's large rooms show objects beyond the game's window under the tiles that hide them on its screen (enhanced.sprite_hidden_frames).

# With the settling camera (profile 2) the black is a few pixels a frame above the previous camera's (enhanced.black_pixels_mean): where Link stops, or walks away from the black past the map's edge, it frames him without the previous camera's look-ahead, its own half as long, and shows a few lines more of that black (9200: 2 px lower at rest; 24840 to 25140: 2 to 4 px behind him); no room still being prepared shows more.
# zoom-out.route in the far view fitted to the screen (--screen): 426x320 on 1280x960, 412x360 on 1240x1080, the rules of its far 4:3 rows.

# With the settling camera (profile 2) the black is a few pixels a frame above the previous camera's (enhanced.black_pixels_mean): where Link stops, or walks away from the black past the map's edge, it frames him without the previous camera's look-ahead, its own half as long, and shows a few lines more of that black (9200: 2 px lower at rest; 24840 to 25140: 2 to 4 px behind him); no room still being prepared shows more.
# zoom-out.route in medium 16:9: the diagonals and corners the band shows when wider than a room.

# With the settling camera (profile 2) the black is a few pixels a frame above the previous camera's (enhanced.black_pixels_mean): where Link stops, or walks away from the black past the map's edge, it frames him without the previous camera's look-ahead, its own half as long, and shows a few lines more of that black (9200: 2 px lower at rest; 24840 to 25140: 2 to 4 px behind him); no room still being prepared shows more.

# intro.route: the night Nayru's possession puts on Lynna (CUTSCENE_NAYRU_SINGING, from 7877 to 15895), which the neighbouring rooms take with the game's window: never a window much darker than the band around it (enhanced.window_darker_frames), the tint only through that scene.

# intro.route: Impa sets GLOBALFLAG_INTRO_DONE in 0:39, whose interaction $6b no longer creates Nayru, Ralph and the animals then: the rooms whose objects read the flag are run again, and the band meets one still drawn with the people of before for 36 frames, Link in the room (enhanced.objects_stale_frames; 947, the room shown with them until the end, when nothing ran it again). 0:39 itself, run from the Maku Tree's room on its left, has the Ralph ($37 $0d) the game creates only for Link coming from there: once Link is in 0:49 below it, it is run again from there, the band meeting it out of date for 12 frames more (48 in all), drawn from the image of the room left meanwhile.

# intro.route: Nayru's picture ends on a white screen, where the scene puts Link back two steps away, and the night ends with his object made anew in the room's corner before he stands again: the camera glided to him and back as the screen faded in (21 frames, 57 to 61 px a row); it is now on him at the first frame that shows (enhanced.return_glide_frames).

# intro.route: the time portal of 0:39, which the game shows one frame in two and animates, turning and flickering in the band as in the room (a capture's object records are read a frame after the OAM kept, so that its visible bit reads hidden on the frame that shows it): 84 objects animated, 80 before, and one left unplaced, two before (enhanced.poses_animated, enhanced.poses_frozen_unplaced).

# intro.route: the rooms whose terrain's key bytes move (Impa's door in 0:3a, 0:49's flags at the scroll's start) are run again kept drawn (enhanced.terrain_refreshes), the band meeting one for 37 frames at most (enhanced.terrain_stale_frames), its neighbours black for 18 frames, 56 when they were thrown. The room in play's own entry is thrown as before when its terrain moves, and the room a scroll left is drawn from its image, never from its entry kept out of date (enhanced.left_stale_frames: 66 frames when it was kept, 0:7a's old terrain drawn behind Link).

# intro.route: each room beside the one Link stands in, against the game's own entry into it from there (--beside-witness): none shows people that entry does not create (0:39 above 0:49 showed the Ralph of its run from the left, two objects, when nothing ran it again from below).

# intro.route: the room a scroll left gives way to the image the game last drew of it, through the scroll and while it stays out of date beside the room entered, when its entry shows objects that read the side it was entered by and was run from another side than the game entered it by: going down from 0:39 to 0:49, its entry run from the Maku Tree's room drew Ralph above Link for 36 frames (25 of the scroll, 11 until the run from below came back); out of the scroll, never in place of an entry that holds for the side (enhanced.left_image_held_frames), nor a room beside Link drawn from an entry out of date for its side (enhanced.side_stale_frames).

# intro.route with the sub-pixel camera, its dialogues in Lynna: the text box shown unmoved over the band moved, the band keeping its fraction as the box opens and closes; where the picture switches (a scroll starting or ending, a text box opening or closing, Link drawn apart or no longer) the band's step changes by 2 px of the screen at most, as elsewhere (enhanced.switch_band_jolt_max), where it dropped its fraction for the scroll before, up to 4 px at once; Link's by 6 at most, his own fraction where he is no longer drawn apart.
# The ghost in its thread holds it as well, paced or not: the tint takes the room's palettes from its entry, delivered before the scene, and needs no run during it.

# intro.route with the rooms never visited kept dark (--unvisited-rooms hidden): a new game, nearly every room around Link unvisited, each fading in at its first entry; the black under the rows' without it.

# The edge fades follow the order the ghost computes the rooms in: with the corners run before a scroll brings them in and the sea's other side chained from the room there, 19 dark rooms' edges fade in (enhanced.edge_fades), 21 before; 17 since the rooms run again for their terrain are kept drawn; never more than 19, the others' pixels there before the band shows them bare.

# intro.route with the rooms never visited kept dark, the view's savestate saved at 4240, Link in 0:59 walking up toward 0:49 never entered, and loaded 120 frames later, once 0:49 is entered and marked: the load brings 0:49 back unvisited and dark at once, the view forgetting the rooms it drew before (without that, 0:49, the reference before the load, would stay drawn in clear unvisited: enhanced.shown_unvisited); Link goes on up into 0:49, so the neighbours of the save never come back (enhanced.reload not pinned).

# The reveal and edge fades are exact counts that follow the order the ghost computes the rooms in: with the corners run before a scroll brings them in, 8 rooms fade in as Link enters them (enhanced.reveal_fades, 7 before) and 24 edges (enhanced.edge_fades, 25 before).

# intro.route with the rooms never visited kept dark in the far 4:3 view of a small console, with the sub-pixel camera; and in the drawn-back view as the Low quality has it (--neighbour-animation off): the edge of the dark rooms cut straight.

# swim.route: the scroll down at 3291, which the doubled scroll's steps once ended a few pixels short of the game's own distance, now ends on it; Link reaches the next edge eight frames sooner (3448) and the replay parts from its recording from there, through 22 transitions, 19 of them swum, where the recording made 25 and 22 (swim-diagonal.route keeps their course, its inputs from 3449 on eight frames earlier). Without the sub-pixel camera (far 4:3, fitted, near) the band steps with his whole steps, 1, 1, 0 on a diagonal as the game does, his sprite steady: its stops between two of them and its steps back across a diagonal (enhanced.band_stops, enhanced.band_wobble) are held at what they are, about a fifth and three fifths above the previous camera's, which moved him on the screen instead.

# swim.route with the sub-pixel camera in far 4:3, its swims at the surface across the rooms' edges: where the picture switches (a scroll starting or ending, a text box opening or closing, Link drawn apart or no longer) the band's step changes by 2 px of the screen at most, as elsewhere (enhanced.switch_band_jolt_max), where it dropped its fraction for the scroll before, up to 4 px at once; Link's by 6 at most (10 before he was drawn apart through the scrolls, where the game moves his sprites itself); his layer coming or going in a scroll no longer moves him against the ground by his own fraction, up to 3 px of the screen 63 times before (enhanced.transition_layer_shift_max). Where the water ripples the band takes its fraction too, Link drawn apart at each line's scroll: at 4x it stops between two of its steps 26 times an axis instead of 116, 23 of them on frames where Link himself stands still on that axis, and goes back across a diagonal by 2 px or more 10 times instead of 48.
# swim.route in the far view fitted to the screen (--screen): 426x320 on 1280x960, 412x360 on 1240x1080, the rules of its far 4:3 rows.

# The settling camera holds the band toward a room still being prepared beside it, so that its path follows the ghosts' rhythm: with the ghosts' new order the band goes back across the walk 84 times (enhanced.band_wobble), 81 before.
# swim.route in the view's other sizes (docs/REFERENCE.md): near in 4:3, medium in 16:9 and 4:3.
# save.route: the game's own save at the end of overworld.route, the same cartridge RAM on both cores (its SHA-1); load.route
# opens that file, on mGBA compared room by room with SameBoy's replay (in room 104, where the file before the save opens

# stairs-diagonal.route: Link down and up the stairs south of the start, then diagonally in 0:7d, written by hand; his sprite as the frame draws it never goes back on the screen against the step before (enhanced.link_backsteps), in every size of the view and with both camera profiles. Without the sub-pixel camera the band steps with his whole steps, as the game does: its stops between two of them (enhanced.band_stops) are held at 29, the previous camera's 20 moving him on the screen instead.
# The first camera profile starts following at its dead zone's edge on a frame Link's sprite does not step: one step back in the first diagonal of 0:7d.
# The first camera profile with the sub-pixel camera switched off and on again during the walk, as Display's Camera from the pause: as before the second profile settled.

# stairs-diagonal.route with the view's savestate saved at 1400 and loaded 120 frames later, the sub-pixel camera switched on at the frame after the load: the camera keeps the reducer's place, not a whole camera's it does not know yet (enhanced.reload_camera_delta).

# stairs-diagonal.route with Link drawn in phase on a diagonal walk (--enhanced-link-phase, a trial, off by default): the stairs, a walk down at half a pixel a frame, are left as they were; in 0:7d's diagonals the camera, its x held at the map's edge, steps back across the walk once as without it (enhanced.camera_wobble), and his sprite never goes back on the screen.

# stairs-diagonal.route with the sub-pixel camera (--enhanced-subpixel, the default on computers, which the harness takes only when asked), as a screen at 4x shows it: the band stops between two of its steps 8 times an axis instead of 20 (enhanced.band_stops), the stairs' half a pixel a frame going by its own speed; Link drawn apart at his exact place.

# stairs-diagonal.route with the sub-pixel camera switched off and on again six times during the walk (--enhanced-subpixel-switch), as Display's Camera from the pause: the band and Link give their fractions back or take them up by 1/16 of a pixel a frame, the camera's whole pixels then the Pixel camera's own; no jolt past the Pixel camera's (a step of 4 px of the screen then none, on the stairs' half a pixel a frame), Link never left in the band nor drawn twice; the band's stops between its steps half way between the two cameras' (8 and 20).

# diagonal-crossings.route: Link crossing the edges of 0:6c, 0:6b and 0:5c diagonally, written by hand; with --continuous-diagonal a diagonal held carries him across the scroll's axis too (transitions.carried_frames), and the frames he stands across it two frames running (enhanced.scroll_across_stalled) are those a wall across holds him, in 0:6b below its middle and along its top row, and along 0:5c's bottom row.

# line-edges.route: the transitions at the line (--continuous-line), written by hand. Two taps toward 0:6c's left edge leave Link at x=1 in the room and the next room unchanged, where the game's own bound would have started the scroll at x=5 (transitions.line_rests); the scrolls start at the line, Link put back on it (transitions.line_clamps); let go during a scroll he stands, the scroll's move undone (transitions.stopped_frames), in the pose the game stands him in with nothing held, but at the frame that ends it, whose pose the game has loaded (transitions.standing_frames), turned back he walks back toward the line (transitions.back_frames), and once it is over he crosses back into the room he left. Without the option the second tap already takes him into 0:6b.

# line-edges.route on foot as the OAM draws him (walk.drawn_off_scroll_frames, the frames of a transition and the 3 after it where his sprites' offset from his place at the frame before moved by a pixel; walk.drawn_off_mid_frames elsewhere): at the frames that start a scroll, where the game's load runs past its vblank, his sprite goes where the game's own step took him, his graphics' entries alone moved, instead of standing a frame and then jumping two pixels; before, 19 frames so of 574, and his sprites zigzagged on 10 (enhanced.link_drawn_zigzags).

# line-corner.route: diagonals through the corner where 0:57, 0:58, 0:67 and 0:68 meet, with the transitions at the line, written by hand. Carried across during a scroll, Link goes on at his pace past the line across into the room beside, its collisions predicted from the ROM's tables, and the scroll into it starts from where he stands at the frame that ends the scroll (transitions.cross_started), three times, where he slowed down to reach the line as the scroll ended before (transitions.carry_edge_frames); each prediction is what the game then loads (transitions.beside_matched). Turned back in the scroll from 0:67 into 0:68, he walks on back past the line into 0:67, on its collisions as normal play had them (transitions.back_past_frames), and the transition back is forced from where he stands as the scroll ends (transitions.back_reversals, transitions.back_forced). The one vertical camera jump is the walk out of the first house, as on swim.route. At the frame that chains the scroll into the room across to the first, the game draws none of Link: he is built from his fields there, inside the game's window too (enhanced.link_chained_frames, enhanced.link_chained_unshown), where he vanished for that frame before.

# line-edges.route with the sub-pixel camera: the camera follows Link through the line's scrolls, stopped and turned back, a frame he stands there not taken for a stop while the scroll goes on. Link as shown dips back by a pixel against his step in a scroll, then on, at no frame (enhanced.scroll_link_dips; once before, an OAM left uncopied drawing his sprites a pixel behind his place while his fraction ran on).

# line-corner-menu.route: the menu opened at the frame after a scroll ends with Link walked back past the line, the transition back raised and not taken: kept while he stands past it (transitions.back_kept_frames), the game taking it from where he stands once the menu closes, none lowered and none put back on the line (transitions.back_lowered, transitions.put_back), no jump of Link's (enhanced.link_jumps), where lowering it left him outside the room and the line's test put him back on it 21 px away. The scroll back into 0:67 starts at the first world frame after the menu, 0:67 drawn whole there; the check takes what the band showed before it from the last world frame, not the framed menu's (enhanced.transitions_black).

# line-corners.route: diagonals through two corners with the transitions at the line, written by hand: the corner of 0:57, 0:58, 0:67 and 0:68, down-left, and the corner of 0:56, 0:57, 0:66 and 0:67, up-left then down-right. Carried across during the first scroll, Link goes on at his pace past the line into the room beside, its collisions predicted from the ROM's tables (its tileset, layout, substitutions and collisions), and the scroll into it starts from where he stands at the frame that ends the first (transitions.cross_started), with no frame of normal play between them; he slowed down to reach the line as the scroll ended before (transitions.carry_edge_frames, 81 then). Up-left into the second corner, from 0:67 left into 0:66, the comedian of 0:56 is no scene: his script waits for the A button before it takes the controls (transitions.beside_scene_rooms). Each room beside predicted is what the game then loads (transitions.beside_matched). A savestate loaded in the second scroll of the last corner gives the same steps (enhanced.reload_transition_differing). At the frame that chains the scroll into the room across to the first, the game draws none of Link: he is built from his fields there, inside the game's window too (enhanced.link_chained_frames, enhanced.link_chained_unshown), where he vanished for that frame before.

# line-corners.route with the sub-pixel camera: at the frame that chains the scroll into the room across to the first, the game draws none of Link, who is built from his fields there, inside the game's window too, in his layer (enhanced.link_chained_frames, none of them without a pixel of him, enhanced.link_chained_unshown); he vanished on that frame before.

# diagonal-crossings.route with Link drawn in phase on a diagonal walk (--enhanced-link-phase): the camera steps back across the walk 12 times in its diagonal frames instead of 51, in the drawn-back view 8 instead of 42, the rest where Link slides along a wall or the camera catches up in the first frames of a walk; the game is the same (the transitions' counts), his sprite never goes back on the screen.

# diagonal-crossings.route with the sub-pixel camera (--enhanced-subpixel): at 4x the band stops between two of its steps 8 times an axis instead of 131 (6 instead of 120 in the drawn-back view), and steps back across the walk by 2 px or more 13 times instead of 49 (10 instead of 40); the game is the same (the transitions' counts).

# swim-diagonal.route: Link swimming at the surface with the mermaid suit across the edge between 0:c4 and 0:b4 diagonally, written by hand; with --continuous-diagonal his motion carries him across the scroll's axis at its own angle and speed, into water (transitions.carried_frames), and he never stands across it (enhanced.scroll_across_stalled); the one vertical camera jump is the start's, swim.route's, with the diagonal or without.

# swim-diagonal.route with the sub-pixel camera (--enhanced-subpixel) in the drawn-back view, Far 16:9 as a 1080p screen shows it at 4x: where the picture switches (a scroll starting or ending, a text box opening or closing, Link drawn apart or no longer) the band's step changes by 2 px of the screen at most, as elsewhere (enhanced.switch_band_jolt_max), where it dropped its fraction for the scroll before, up to 4 px at once; Link's by 6 at most, and he is drawn apart through the scrolls, never moving against the ground by his own fraction there (enhanced.transition_layer_shift_max); the game is the same. Where the water ripples the band takes its fraction too, Link drawn apart at each line's scroll: at 4x the band stops between two of its steps 26 times an axis instead of 65 and goes back across the swim by 2 px or more 15 times instead of 25.
# The transitions' steps (--continuous-steps, which the home screen turns on with them): Link takes a step a frame of the game
# through a transition as the keys give it.  The frame whose logic ends a scroll gives him his step (transitions.end_steps), where
# without them it left him still a frame (transitions.end_stalls, on diagonal-crossings 12 of 13), and the frame that starts a
# diagonal one completes the game's own step instead of adding one across (transitions.doubled_starts); on foot, with no direction
# held toward the edge, from the frame it is let go he goes evenly as far as the game takes him, without walking

# swim-line.route: Link swimming at the surface with the mermaid suit, the transitions at the line. Every frame of normal play the policy's step of his swim is the game's own (transitions.swim_model_mismatched=0), and through each scroll he swims by that step and nothing else: a glide let go at an edge, crossing it, goes exactly as far as the same glide in the middle of a room (swim.edge_glides_unlike=0, swim.edge_glide_off_max=0), where the forced swim once took him 15 or 16 px whatever his speed. A swim that crosses a line, a direction held toward it or not, starts the scroll the frame before, never put back on the line (3438, the key let go as he crosses). Of the scroll frames, those he goes otherwise than his motion are walls and land the game holds him at as well (0:97's wall at x=80, 18 frames; 0:b4's shore, 19) and one frame the game's own load ran past its vblank (1880). The corner of 0:a4, 0:a5, 0:b4 and 0:b5 carries him past the line across into 0:b4, its scroll started from where he swims (transitions.cross_started); turned back in the scroll into 0:b5 he swims back past the line, the scroll back started at the frame that ends it (transitions.back_reversals). He stands on a room's first column at the left line on 50 frames, drawn whole (enhanced.link_left_line_frames). The same rooms on both cores.

# seafloor-line.route: Link on Ages' sea floor in his mermaid suit, the transitions at the line. His suit's step is the game's own at every frame of normal play (transitions.swim_model_mismatched=0), a wall's stop included; through each scroll he goes by that step, his walk animated with a direction held and standing without one: a tap at an edge, which once pushed him 15 px at speed 0 (2561 on the session it comes from), glides him as in the middle of a room (swim.edge_glides_unlike=0). At the corner of 2165 the room beside, a sea floor's, is foreseen (transitions.beside_predicted, the same as the game's once loaded: beside_mismatched=0), and his move across goes on at his pace into it (transitions.carry_edge_frames=0); the route then takes other rooms than it was recorded in, its later taps away from the edges. Of the scroll frames, those he goes otherwise than his motion: the wall of 0:97 at the surface, and one frame the game's load ran past its vblank (the scroll's end then counted a stall, transitions.end_stalls=1). Turned back in a scroll into 2:a6, he goes back past the line into 2:a5, the scroll back started at the frame that ends it. He stands on the room's first column at the left line on 4 frames, drawn whole (enhanced.link_left_line_frames); as the frame draws him he follows his place through every scroll as in the middle of a room (swim.drawn_off_scroll_frames=0, of swim.drawn_scroll_frames). The same rooms on both cores.

# swim-corners.route: Link at the surface of Ages' sea in his mermaid suit, then on its floor and back up, diagonals held across the edges and the corners of 0:a4, 0:a5, 0:b4 and 0:b5 again and again. As the OAM draws him he follows his place through every scroll as in the middle of a room (swim.drawn_off_scroll_frames, of swim.drawn_scroll_frames, the frames of a transition and the 3 after it where his sprites' offset from his place at the frame before moved by a pixel, against swim.drawn_off_mid_frames elsewhere): at the frames that start a scroll, where the game's load runs past its vblank, his sprite goes where the game's own step took him, as it follows the policy's, his own graphics' entries alone moved, never a splash beside him; on the room's left line just after a scroll, both his columns are drawn, in one layer. Before, 80 frames of the 1354 moved so, 0 elsewhere. Drawn from his fields past the window's edge, he stands where the OAM would have him too (swim.drawn_off_built_frames, 141 before), his sprites steady (enhanced.link_drawn_zigzags). On the sea floor the band goes on drawing the waves through a scroll the game stops them for, their lines a pixel short of the band's right edge here and there (4270, 4553 on): a ripple's fringe, as in play, counted with the ripples (enhanced.black_other_frames, none). At the end, a scroll up out of 0:b4 he swims back down in turns back at once from where he stands, under the line of the room above (transitions.back_reversals), instead of a frame of normal play there taking him out of the water and walking him through the scroll down (swim.walked_scroll_frames, 26 before; swim.left_water_past_room); a glide too slow to leave those rows is carried over the line by the scroll's end (transitions.swim_lifted_frames, 7 frames before the corners kept their pace, none on the path since). On the sea floor the rooms beside are foreseen (transitions.beside_predicted, none different from the game's load); across 0:a5, whose own code changes two of its tiles, they are foreseen too, its code replayed, and the carry across keeps its pace (transitions.carry_edge_frames, 85 before). That path ends the scroll up from 0:b5 into 0:a5 (3214) against a wall straight ahead: the swim's model of the step at the scroll's end holds him whole for a frame the game still steps him 2 px to the wall, then slides him along it (transitions.end_stalls), as seafloor-steps and seafloor-line already have a frame short of a shore.
